verdict: Caution: lend selectively to Erode dyeing/processing units with captive effluent treatment and diversified buyer books; avoid job-work-only units with single-buyer dependence and no ZLD compliance.
title: Erode textile dyeing & processing: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
A dyeing or processing house takes grey fabric or yarn, runs it through wet processes — scouring, bleaching, dyeing, finishing — and sells finished fabric or job-work services. Cash comes in per metre processed or per kg dyed, so the unit is a conversion machine: throughput times realisation minus dye, chemical, power, water and labour cost. So when a proposal lands, check the split between own-fabric sale and job-work — job-work earns a fixed conversion charge with no pricing power, and that is where margin vanishes first.

## What has changed now
Tamil Nadu GST collections are running -3.2% Apr-to-date against India +6.1%, a 9.3 pp gap and a genuine local demand signal [D]. Nationally IIP for textiles (NIC 13) is +13.1% YoY and +11.9% Apr-to-date, with bank credit +14.6% — so the national picture is fine and the state picture is not [D]. **The gap is the story: Erode's order book is softer than the all-India textile print suggests.** Locally, a state-wide dyeing mills strike was called for October 5, halting processing across the belt including Perundurai SIPCOT [3]; a weavers' wage-hike announcement is pending in Erode [2]. Both are cost and continuity events, not demand events. Peer results are mixed: Arvind's Q2 FY27 net profit rose 44% to Rs 148 crore on revenue of Rs 2,919 crore, up 23% [6], while Sportking's operating margin jumped to 19% in Q1 FY27 from 12% after a weak FY24-FY26 stretch at 6-10% [7]. **Read peers as proof that scale and integration earn margin; small standalone processors do not.**

## Where the growth is
Pursue processors who have moved up from job-work to own-fabric supply for exporters, and units with in-house ZLD and captive power — the 2026 waste rules pushing non-recyclable textile waste into RDF raise compliance cost for everyone and favour those already compliant [4]. **The borrower to back is the one whose buyer list has three or more named exporters and whose ETP is running, not the one with the cheapest rate.** Avoid pure job-work units with one buyer above half of turnover, and any unit whose effluent consent is under renewal.

## How to grow safely
Structure against the conversion cycle, not the balance sheet. Take monthly: GST returns, power bills (units consumed, not rupees), ETP running logs, and a buyer-wise sales statement. Collect from customer: current capacity utilisation, water sourcing cost, and effluent consent validity.

## Early warning signs
Watch power consumption per metre — a fall without a sales fall means the machines are idle. Watch GST turnover against bank credits; a widening gap means sales are being routed elsewhere. **If a unit misses a wage payment in the week the weavers' wage hike is announced [2], treat it as a liquidity event and re-price.** Strike or shutdown news in the Perundurai belt [3] is a direct cash-flow interruption — check the buffer before it happens, not after.
